newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds resume bid tone post-tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds resume bid tone post-tender.

text.p: *Australian bonds found a more positive tone following a well received A$600 million T-bond tender and after merchandise imports for October showed only a modest rise
*U.S. Treasuries also face supply later today
Australian bonds found a more positive tone on Tuesday on a well received T-bond tender and after merchandise imports for October showed only a modest rise.

Traders said A$600 million of long-dated supply had weighed on the market at the start fo the week, stemming the recent strong rally, but both tranches attracted a tight range of bids and had been in demand after following recent offshore buying.
The A$200 million of November 2006 bonds, the current 10-year benchmark, went off at a yield of 7.144 percent, while the A$400 million of September 2009 fetched 7.277 percent.
The yield on the benchmark bond eased to 7.11 percent by the close compared with around 7.16 percent when tender bids went in and after rising to near 7.20 percent in early trading.
Imports rose 1.0 percent in October, just a shade over median expectations, and included a 1.0 percent fall in consumer goods and a 7.0 percent drop in capital goods imports.

"The trend weakness in imports is indicative of easing domestic demand growth and reinforces our view that there will be another cut in official interest rates early in the New Year," said Stephen McNabb, an economist at Westpac.
March 1997 bill futures firmed to 93.80 after a recent softer tone, indicating a cash rate of 6.20 percent by maturity.
Official rates were last cut to 6.50 percent on November 6.

However, Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia, said the data suggested the economy was not heading for recession and there was no certainty rates would be eased again. "If there are further signs that the economy is holding a 2.5-3.0 percent pace at the low point of the cycle, which is occuring now, then the scope for a further rate cut and further bond market bullishness is limited," he added.
Bond yield spreads narrowed sharply against the U.S. and Canada, but New Zealand's spread to Australia narrowed slightly after August quarter earnings came in lower than expected.
The U.S. faces a US$18.25 billion auction of 2-year notes later today and US$12.5 billion of 5-year notes on Wednesday.

The firm tone saw the 10-year bond contract snap back through resistance at 92.830 and 92.860 and now needs to overcome 92.920 to resume the rally through 92.950, the 33-month peak seen last week. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
